sanity_expectations: Speed sqrt(vx^2+vy^2) decays monotonically over time due to combined linear, nonlinear, and saturating drag (no external drive to the energy)
vx and vy oscillate (rotate) with decaying amplitude — quasi-circular spiral-in in the (vx,vy) plane
Instantaneous angular frequency is modulated in time via delta_omega*sin(omega_mod*t), so oscillation spacing varies slightly
All trajectories remain finite and bounded for t in [0,30]
Initial condition dvx_dt(0) < 0 (drag terms dominate since vy=0 kills the gyration terms)
excitation_report: ODE-mode excitation_check (full child-vs-parent systems on the target vx trajectory): the NEW saturating-drag term -gamma_sat*vx/(1+(vx^2+vy^2)/v_star^2) reaches a max effect of 1.31 on dvx_dt = 26.2*sigma (sigma=0.05), strongest at t~4.7 — well above the 5*sigma threshold. Initial speed=3, so (vx^2+vy^2)/v_star^2 ~ 2.25 at start, keeping the saturating drag in its partially-saturated regime (distinguishable from constant gamma_drag). Dominant gyration term omega*vy ~ O(3) and modulation term kappa_cycl*(omega_field0+delta_omega*sin)*vy are both large and clearly visible; the other dissipative terms (gamma_drag, beta_nl, alpha_hall) act steadily over the 0-30 window as the orbit spirals in.

scenario_text: A charged particle enters a region of uniform magnetic field oriented perpendicular to its initial velocity. The magnetic force continuously turns the velocity vector without changing its speed, producing circular motion in the plane. We track the two in-plane velocity components as they evolve over time. The strength of the field and the charge-to-mass ratio set the turning rate.
